Microsoft reports $24.1 billion in OpenAI-related revenue, including revenue-sharing payments, for July 2025–June 2026; this is neither a pure compute figure nor a sector-wide AI revenue share [e2]. These items do not settle either 'vast majority' assertion or the financing dependence asserted for January–June 2026 [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of hyperscaler AI revenues come from Anthropic's and OpenAI's compute spend, which depends on near-perpetual funding, just as the vast majority of Anthropic's and OpenAI's revenues come from AI startups that depend on near-perpetual funding to keep spending.

statement.excerpt: The vast majority of hyperscaler AI revenues come from Anthropic and OpenAI’s compute spend that is dependent on near-perpetual funding, much like the vast majority of Anthropic and OpenAI’s revenues come from AI startups that depend on near-perpetual funding to continue their spend.

from_speaker: vast majority of hyperscaler AI revenues
vast majority of Anthropic and OpenAI’s revenues
our_interpretation: The claim has two revenue-concentration assertions and a financing-dependence assertion for each layer. All must hold for full support.
The plain reading of 'vast majority' is an overwhelming share, substantially above half. No exact percentage is imposed.
Treat hyperscalers as the major commercial cloud providers discussed in the post, including Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Oracle.
Read the two labs' revenue share on a combined basis; do not replace total revenue with API revenue or enterprise revenue.
Read 'near-perpetual funding' as an ongoing need for repeated external financing to sustain the spending, not literal proof about eternity.
Use January–June 2026, the latest common financial reporting window described in the post. Later monthly spending samples are context.
Treat the shares as estimates, consistent with the post's use of spending samples and reported figures.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable revenue breakdowns show overwhelming concentration at both layers, and cash-flow evidence shows that the relevant spending materially requires repeated external financing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable breakdowns show a substantial majority of either revenue pool comes from other customer groups, or cash-flow records show the asserted financing dependence does not hold.
